name: Stratechery
bio: Ben Thompson's weekly Stratechery newsletter remains required reading for tech and media strategy. Each essay untangles the economics of platforms (Apple, Google, Meta, Microsoft) with framework-grade clarity. Paid tier adds the Stratechery Plus weekly podcast and private Discord.

name: Doomberg
bio: Anonymous macro newsletter from a former energy-industry insider. Doomberg dissects commodities, central-bank policy, and the energy transition with sharp charts and no-vendor takes. Particularly good on oil, natural gas, and the shenanigans of ESG capitalism. Free on Substack.

name: The Bear Cave
bio: Edwin Dorsey's weekly short-selling due diligence letter. Each issue profiles a public-company accounting concern, governance red flag, or business-model crack. Paid; trial issues and the David vs Goliath Twitter thread are public.

name: MacroVoices Weekly Digest
bio: Patrick Ceresna's long-form interview podcast with hedge-fund managers, CIOs, and macro strategists. The weekly digest email rounds up recent episodes and links to charts and transcripts. Free; also offers a paid Dark Side of the Hedge Fund series.

name: Topdown Charts
bio: Callum Thomas' macro research on the go. Topdown Charts pairs clean charts with short commentary on liquidity, central-bank policy, and risk-asset crosses. Daily free chart email plus the paid Weekly Macro Letter.

name: The Kobeissi Letter
bio: Adam Kobeissi's daily markets letter covering crude oil, FX, equities, and commodities. Read by traders, hedge funds, and front-office desks for intraday takes and chart analysis. Paid subscription; sometimes sparked by a Reddit thread he started.

name: Geopolitical Futures
bio: Founded by George Friedman, Geopolitical Futures is a forecasting subscription that maps risk across the major theaters — US, China, Middle East, Europe — with weekly long-form reports and a shorter-form daily note.

name: Outside the Box (Mauldin Economics)
bio: John Mauldin's curated weekly macro letter, edited by his team. Each issue synthesizes a dozen outside sources — bond desks, central-bank notes, geopolitical dispatches — into one brief. Required reading for cross-asset allocators.

name: Barron's Daily (Stock Alert)
bio: Bloomberg Markets' daily newsletter covering what's moving equity, bond, FX, and commodity markets — and why. Free with a Bloomberg account. The desk often co-broadcasts live on the same theme with publishers past and present including Matt Levine.

name: The Daily Shot
bio: Alexander Crawford's daily markets chart email. One clean chart each morning with a short blurb explaining what it means for the session ahead. Free; mirror accounts on Twitter and LinkedIn.

name: Finimize
bio: Daily 3-minute briefing explaining one finance headline in plain English. Free email and app. Widely read by career-changers and early-career bankers; longer-form explainers live on the site. Now backed by Abrdn.

name: Mish Talk
bio: Mike Shedlock's blog and newsletter, bent on contrarian macro takes. Tracks Federal Reserve policy, the bond market, and sentiment shifts with daily posts. Long-running back-catalog useful for context and citation.

name: Bear Traps Report
bio: Larry McDonald's weekly macro cross-asset letter. Ex-bank analyst turned publisher; widely cited by hedge funds and family offices. Paid; covers rates, FX, commodities, and credit in one place, with occasional podcasts and event commentary.

name: Apollo Slok — Thinking Things Over
bio: Torsten Slok, Apollo's chief economist, publishes a weekly charts-of-the-week report on global macro, rates, and Fed-policy cross-currents. Free at Apollo's insights page and through Apollo's institutional email list, with a bonus deck attached.

name: Hindenburg Research
bio: Nathan Anderson's short-selling research firm. Publishes forensic short reports on US-listed companies with governance, fraud, or business-model concerns. Their reports routinely move names intraday, including the 2023-2024 moves on Adani and Icahn Enterprises.

name: Variant Perception
bio: Vincent Deluard's paid institutional macro research service. Frequent cross-asset calls on equities, rates, FX, and commodities, anchored in a 'providers-of-liquidity' framework. Subscribers include sovereign-wealth funds and macro hedge funds, plus long-only desks.

name: Platformer
bio: Casey Newton's subscription on how big tech meets the public interest. Daily pieces on platforms, AI, content moderation, and the creator economy. Required reading in DC, Brussels, and Bay-Away corridor board rooms.

name: Lenny's Newsletter
bio: Lenny Rachitsky (formerly Airbnb) publishes every two weeks on growth, product management, hiring, and SaaS metrics. Free on Substack; one of the largest product-management communities on the open web, with regular webinars and Q&A threads.

name: The Pragmatic Engineer
bio: Gergely Orosz's deep dive on the software engineering profession. Big-tech cultures, EU vs US engineering orgs, careers, and the platform economy. One of the few publications quoted by senior engineers.

name: ByteByteGo
bio: Alex Xu (formerly Alibaba and Microsoft) writes illustrated system-design tutorials. Each issue breaks down one distributed-systems pattern with diagrams. Companion site for his bestselling 'System Design Interview' book series and the paid System Design School course.

name: Import AI
bio: Jack Clark (Anthropic co-founder) compiles the week's biggest AI research papers, model releases, and policy moves. Free; widely cited by AI labs and safety researchers as a Friday-morning must-read, with a politics-of-AI angle baked in.

name: Growth.Design
bio: Jon Snow's weekly teardowns of product onboarding, pricing pages, and growth surfaces. Free; popular with PMs and designers wanting real before-and-after design walkthroughs. Best for the first month of a new designer's onboarding.

name: Demand Curve
bio: Paid growth-and-marketing course library plus a weekly digest. Teaches paid acquisition, lifecycle, and conversion-rate optimization. Built by growth operators; widely cited on Twitter and LinkedIn, with detailed case studies and templated playbooks.

name: The Information
bio: Premium subscription tech news outlet founded by Jessica Lessin. Daily morning briefings on AI, semiconductors, and platform shifts, plus long-form investigations. A must-read across VCs and tech execs; paywalled since launch.

name: Fintech Brainfood
bio: Simon Taylor's weekly fintech digest. Combines product teardowns with deep dives on payments, embedded finance, and the platform banking stack. Free on Substack; the podcast is optional but worth the bonus episodes.

name: Benedict Evans
bio: Independent tech analyst's annual letter and shorter weekly notes. Covers the macro shape of the tech industry — AI, smartphones, platforms, and computing cycles. His 'Three Eras of Computing' essay set a benchmark for the AI era.

name: Daring Fireball
bio: John Gruber's weekly Apple-and-tech opinion blog. Famous for live-blogging Apple keynotes; his link-summarizing style, in which he curates and links to outside pieces with commentary, has shaped a generation of tech writing.

name: The Neuron
bio: Daily AI newsletter with three short stories each morning plus a weekend deep dive. Free; popular with AI-curious professionals outside the tech industry. Also known as 'The Neuron Daily', with email-grade readability.

name: The Defiant
bio: Camila Faber's daily crypto coverage. Now covers the full stack: protocols, regulation, stablecoins, on-chain alpha, and restaking. Free email; the Defiant Show podcast ships three nights a week, with archive of guests going back years.

name: Milk Road
bio: Casual daily crypto briefing written for non-coders. Each issue opens with one core story, follows up with three smaller news bites, and ends with a glossary entry. Free; the team also publishes longer explainers on the site.

name: Bankless
bio: Ryan Sean Adams and David Hoffman's flagship crypto newsletter. Long-form essays on Ethereum, DeFi, rollups, and the on-chain future. Free weekly with a paid tier that unlocks the Rollup podcast.

name: Crypto Pragmatist
bio: Joe Carlasare's commentary on Bitcoin and crypto adoption through the lens of a retirement-account investor and entrepreneur. Conservative sound-money framing plus regular interviews with Bitcoin builders and miners, plus policy takes.

name: The Bitcoin Layer
bio: Weekly newsletter by Nik Bhatia (USC Marshall professor, author of 'Layered Money' and 'Bitcoin Age'). Reads Bitcoin through the lens of a monetary system, layering the macro liquidity backdrop onto on-chain structure. Free with paid tier that unlocks the TBL Liquidity Framework and live calls.

name: Glassnode Insights
bio: Weekly on-chain analytics notes from Glassnode. Covers BTC and ETH flows, derivatives, realized caps, exchange reserves, and ETF flow dashboards. Widely cited by institutional desks and cited by BTC-OPEC narratives.

name: Messari Newsletter
bio: Messari's flagship daily/weekly research email. Token unlocks, regulatory moves, and sector deep-dives (DeFi, AI-x-crypto, RWAs). Free summary with the paid Hub offering dashboards, analyst calls to institutions, and the Annual Messari Report PDF.

name: GZERO Daily
bio: Ian Bremmer's geopolitics brief, mailed each weekday morning. Short takes with a 'global power map' framing — Russia, China, US elections, and the Global South — plus a short companion video.

name: Foreign Affairs Today
bio: Foreign Affairs magazine's daily and weekly note. Picks one piece of analysis off the site (long-form review essay, regional case study) plus a list of the week's top reads. Free email signup; full archive behind paywall.

name: Morning Brew
bio: Morning Brew's weekday newsletter covering business, markets, tech, and culture in a snarky-to-the-point voice. Five-minute read; widely cited by Gen-Z and early-career knowledge workers. Now part of a broader media group.

name: Axios Today
bio: Axios's flagship AM brief. Five short stories across business, politics, tech, and world written in the Axios 'Smart Brevity' style. Free; sponsored at the bottom. Now joined by AI Today, Markets, and Climate Brief variants.

name: The Economist Espresso
bio: The Economist's daily morning brief. Five short takes — one global macro, one US, one Asia, one Europe/MENA, one culture/curiosity. Five-minute read; subscription required for full archive and the companion app.

name: The Cipher Brief
bio: Former senior US national-security officials turned publishers. Weekly notes on the hot theaters (Iran, China, Russia, the Arctic) plus long-form expert interviews. Widely read across Washington think tanks and intelligence-community veterans.
